# link-rss-measurement.txt
#
# Purpose: the raw measurement backing scripts/fleet_build.py's
# FLEET_BUILD_MIN_FREE_MB default (EN.ticket.fleet-build-permit-wrapper, task 1).
#
# The admission question the wrapper answers is "is there room for one more
# linker", i.e. the PEAK resident set size of a single build invocation --
# not the aggregate RSS of many concurrent rustc jobs. So the number below is
# the "maximum resident set size" field from `/usr/bin/time -l`, taken across
# TWO runs of the full `cargo build --release` for this workspace (25 crates
# in this workspace's own dependency graph, ~345 with third-party deps):
#
#   1. warm tree (only a few crates needed recompiling)
#   2. `cargo clean`ed tree (full workspace rebuild)
#
# Both runs report closely matching peak RSS (~1.35 GiB / ~1.41 GiB), which
# is expected: `/usr/bin/time -l`'s reported "maximum resident set size" for
# the `cargo build --release` invocation is the max RSS seen across cargo
# itself and every rustc/linker child process cargo spawned and reaped
# (kernel-accumulated RUSAGE_CHILDREN, folded into the parent's own reported
# rusage on exit) -- so a warm build that still has to link the changed
# crates' final binaries sees essentially the same link-step peak as a full
# rebuild, even though it compiles far less.
#
# ============================================================

# ============================================================
# CHOSEN CONSTANT: FLEET_BUILD_MIN_FREE_MB = 2048
# ============================================================
#
# Arithmetic, from peak RSS to threshold:
#
#   peak "maximum resident set size" observed  = 1441366016 bytes  (run 1, the higher of the two)
#   in MiB (bytes / 1048576)                    = 1374.65 MiB
#   safety margin (measurement variance + other = x1.5
#     concurrent processes on the box; this is
#     a peak-of-two-runs number on an otherwise
#     idle machine, not a worst case)
#   1374.65 MiB * 1.5                           = 2061.97 MiB
#   rounded down to a clean value                = 2048 MiB (2 GiB)
#
# FLEET_BUILD_MIN_FREE_MB = 2048
#
# This is the "room for one more linker" threshold: the wrapper's memory gate
# requires at least this many MB free before admitting a build, re-checked at
# every dequeue attempt (task 3), not once at enqueue.
#
# ============================================================
# WHY macOS "free pages" ALONE IS MISLEADING (and what the wrapper reads instead)
# ============================================================
#
# The operator's 2026-09-01 23:38 measurement showed 2.7G free WITH a 6G
# compressor and large swap counters -- i.e. "free" pages alone read low even
# though several more GB were readily reclaimable. This machine's own
# `vm_stat` right now shows the same shape:
#
#   Pages free:        135406   (x 16384-byte pages = ~2.07 GiB)
#   Pages inactive:     727163   (x 16384-byte pages = ~11.10 GiB, reclaimable
#                                 without swapping -- these are clean/backed
#                                 pages the kernel drops under pressure before
#                                 ever touching swap or the compressor)
#   Pages purgeable:      1401   (negligible here, but also reclaimable on demand)
#
# Reading ONLY "Pages free" would report ~2.07 GiB free on a machine that
# actually has far more readily available -- exactly the operator's 2.7G
# reading, which was itself misleading. So `fleet_build.py`'s memory reader
# (task 3) sums `vm_stat`'s "Pages free" + "Pages inactive" (both reclaimable
# without swap activity) as its "available memory" estimate, rather than
# "Pages free" alone. "Pages purgeable" and swap-compressor internals are
# left out deliberately: they are a much smaller share on this machine and
# folding in compressor accounting risks *overstating* headroom right before
# a page-out event, which is the opposite of the failure this gate exists to
# prevent.
